We will describe the solution space of the equation $$ \left[\begin{array}{rrr} 2 \amp 0 \amp 2 \\ 4 \amp -1 \amp 6 \\ 1 \amp 3 \amp -5 \\ \end{array}\right] \xvec = \left[\begin{array}{r} 0 \\ -5 \\ 15 \end{array}\right]. $$

By [prop-matrix-eq-solution], this equation may be equivalently expressed as $$ x_1\left[\begin{array}{r}2\\4\\1\end{array}\right] + x_2\left[\begin{array}{r}0\\-1\\3\end{array}\right]+ x_3\left[\begin{array}{r}2\\6\\-5\end{array}\right]= \left[\begin{array}{r}0\\-5\\15\end{array}\right] $$ , which is the linear system corresponding to the augmented matrix $$ \left[\begin{array}{rrr|r} 2 \amp 0 \amp 2 \amp 0 \\ 4 \amp -1 \amp 6 \amp -5 \\ 1 \amp 3 \amp -5 \amp 15 \\ \end{array} \right] $$ . The reduced row echelon form of the augmented matrix is $$ \left[\begin{array}{rrr|r} 2 \amp 0 \amp 2 \amp 0 \\ 4 \amp -1 \amp 6 \amp -5 \\ 1 \amp 3 \amp -5 \amp 15 \\ \end{array} \right] \sim \left[\begin{array}{rrr|r} 1 \amp 0 \amp 1 \amp 0 \\ 0 \amp 1 \amp -2 \amp 5 \\ 0 \amp 0 \amp 0 \amp 0 \\ \end{array} \right], $$ which corresponds to the linear system $$ \begin{alignedat}{4} x_1 \amp \amp \amp {}+{} \amp x_3 \amp {}={} \amp 0 \\ \amp \amp x_2 \amp {}-{} \amp 2x_3 \amp {}={} \amp 5. \\ \end{alignedat} $$ The variable $x_3$ is free so we may write the solution space parametrically as $$ \begin{aligned} x_1 \amp {}={} -x_3 \\ x_2 \amp {}={} 5+2x_3. \\ \end{aligned} $$

Since we originally asked to describe the solutions to the equation $A\xvec = \bvec$, we will express the solution in terms of the vector $\xvec$: $$ \xvec =\left[ \begin{array}{r} x_1 \\ x_2 \\ x_3 \end{array} \right] = \left[ \begin{array}{r} -x_3 \\ 5 + 2x_3 \\ x_3 \end{array} \right] =\left[\begin{array}{r}0\\5\\0\end{array}\right] +x_3\left[\begin{array}{r}-1\\2\\1\end{array}\right] $$ As before, we call this a parametric description of the solution space.

This shows that the solutions $\xvec$ may be written in the form $\vvec + x_3\wvec$, for appropriate vectors $\vvec$ and $\wvec$. Geometrically, the solution space is a line in $\real^3$ through $\vvec$ moving parallel to $\wvec$.
